q: What if the CBAM default value table shows a dash for my product from India?
title: When India's CBAM default value is a dash
short: Then the declarant must use the value from the table for other countries and territories in the same annex. A dash means the Commission found no reliable India data for that good. For India this applies to low-carbon ferro-chrome, calcined clay and some hydraulic cements.
audience: Indian exporters whose CN code has no India-specific default value

sections.h: India entries shown as a dash

p: The authorised CBAM declarant uses the other countries and territories value for that CN code. Where the country of production of a precursor is unknown, Annex IV gives the highest default values, which must be used instead.
Offer a verified actual figure. For goods without an India value, the fallback is rarely favourable, so measured data has the most value here.

senseible: Senseible reads coal, coke, gas, electricity and freight invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so an actual figure you send an EU buyer can be traced back to the documents behind it. It does not file CBAM declarations.

sources.label: European Commission, Guidance No. 3, CBAM methods for the calculation of emissions embedded in goods (14 August 2026), section 4.10
